---
title: "West Africa UTCI-Mortality: Gold-Standard Case-Crossover DLNM Analysis"
subtitle: "Objectives 1–4 | Lag 7, Lag 14 and Lag 21 E3_L3 comparison"
author: "Reproducible epidemiological analysis"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"

output:

    number_sections: true

  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    number_sections: true
    fig_caption: true

params:
  analysis_file: "mortality_health_analysis_readydata.rds"

  candidate_lags:
    - 7
    - 14
    - 21

  exposure_df: 3
  lag_df: 3

  mc_draws: 10000

  seed: 20260902

  mmt_lower_quantile: 0.05
  mmt_upper_quantile: 0.95

  min_centre_deaths: 50
  max_kappa: 500

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # PRIMARY LAG IS INTENTIONALLY NULL.
  #
  # Review:
  #   1. cumulative RR comparison
  #   2. lag-response curves
  #   3. 3D surfaces
  #   4. diagnostic table
  #   5. lag 15–21 incremental effects
  #
  # Then manually select ONE:
  #
  # PRIMARY_LAG <- 7
  # PRIMARY_LAG <- 14
  # PRIMARY_LAG <- 21
  #
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  primary_lag: null

```{r}


analysis_file <- params$analysis_file

if (!file.exists(analysis_file)) {

  possible_files <- c(
    "mortality_health_analysis_readydata.rds",
    "mortality_health_analysis_readydata.csv",
    "analysis_ready_matrix.rds"
  )

  found <- possible_files[file.exists(possible_files)]

  if (length(found) == 0) {
    stop(
      "Could not find the processed analytical dataset.\n",
      "Expected: ", analysis_file
    )
  }

  analysis_file <- found[1]
}

if (grepl("\\.rds$", analysis_file, ignore.case = TRUE)) {

  analysis_ready_matrix <- readRDS(analysis_file)

} else if (grepl("\\.csv$", analysis_file, ignore.case = TRUE)) {

  analysis_ready_matrix <- readr::read_csv(
    analysis_file,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

} else {

  stop(
    "Unsupported analytical data format: ",
    analysis_file
  )
}

analysis_ready_matrix <- as_tibble(analysis_ready_matrix)

cat(
  "Analytical dataset imported successfully.\n",
  "Rows: ", nrow(analysis_ready_matrix), "\n",
  "Columns: ", ncol(analysis_ready_matrix), "\n"
)
```

6. Basic structural validation

```{r}
dat <- analysis_ready_matrix

if (!inherits(dat$date, "Date")) {
  dat$date <- as.Date(dat$date)
}

if (!all(dat$outcome %in% c(0, 1), na.rm = TRUE)) {
  stop("`outcome` must be coded 0/1.")
}

if (anyDuplicated(
  dat %>%
    distinct(stratum_id, date)
)) {

  stop(
    "Duplicate stratum_id/date combinations detected."
  )

}

stratum_qc <- dat %>%
  group_by(stratum_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_cases = sum(outcome == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_referents = sum(outcome == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unique_dates = n_distinct(date),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bad_strata <- stratum_qc %>%
  filter(
    n_cases != 1 |
    n_referents < 1 |
    n_unique_dates != n_rows
  )

if (nrow(bad_strata) > 0) {

  warning(
    nrow(bad_strata),
    " strata failed structural case-crossover checks."
  )

}

```

7. Analytical sample definition

The longest candidate lag is 21 days. Therefore all three candidate models are evaluated on the same complete-case analytical population wherever possible.

This avoids comparing models on different mortality strata.

```{r}

model_data <- dat %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(outcome),
    !is.na(stratum_id),
    !is.na(utci_lag0),
    !is.na(utci_lag7),
    !is.na(utci_lag14),
    !is.na(utci_lag21)
  ) %>%
  arrange(stratum_id, date)

if (nrow(model_data) == 0) {
  stop("No observations remain after analytical exposure completeness filtering.")
}

if (n_distinct(model_data$stratum_id) < 10) {
  stop("Fewer than 10 case-crossover strata remain.")
}

cat(
  "Complete analytical dataset:\n",
  "Rows = ", nrow(model_data), "\n",
  "Strata = ", n_distinct(model_data$stratum_id), "\n",
  "Deaths = ", sum(model_data$outcome == 1), "\n"
)
```

18. IMPORTANT: robust DLNM coefficient extraction

This section specifically fixes the error you encountered.

Your diagnostic showed:

crossbasis:
v1.l1 ... v5.l4

gnm:
cbv1.l1 ... cbv5.l4

Thus the 20 coefficients are present and correct, but their names contain the cb prefix added by the model formula.

We therefore do not ask crosspred() to discover them automatically from the gnm object.

Instead:

identify all crossbasis columns;
identify corresponding gnm coefficients;
remove the cb prefix;
reorder them exactly as the crossbasis;
reorder vcov;
pass coef and vcov explicitly.

```{r}
extract_crossbasis_parameters <- function(
    cb,
    fit,
    prefix = "cb"
) {

  cb_names <- colnames(cb)

  if (is.null(cb_names)) {
    stop("Crossbasis has no column names.")
  }

  model_coef <- stats::coef(fit)
  model_names <- names(model_coef)

  expected_model_names <-
    paste0(prefix, cb_names)

  missing_coef <- setdiff(
    expected_model_names,
    model_names
  )

  if (length(missing_coef) > 0) {

    stop(
      "The fitted model does not contain all expected crossbasis ",
      "coefficients.\nMissing:\n",
      paste(missing_coef, collapse = "\n")
    )

  }

  beta <- model_coef[
    expected_model_names
  ]

  names(beta) <- cb_names

  V <- stats::vcov(fit)

  if (is.null(rownames(V)) ||
      is.null(colnames(V))) {

    stop(
      "Model variance-covariance matrix has no coefficient names."
    )

  }

  V_cb <- V[
    expected_model_names,
    expected_model_names,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  rownames(V_cb) <- cb_names
  colnames(V_cb) <- cb_names

  if (length(beta) != ncol(cb)) {

    stop(
      "Crossbasis coefficient length mismatch: ",
      length(beta),
      " coefficients for ",
      ncol(cb),
      " crossbasis columns."
    )

  }

  if (!identical(names(beta), cb_names)) {

    stop(
      "Crossbasis coefficient ordering is not identical to basis ordering."
    )

  }

  if (!isTRUE(all.equal(
    rownames(V_cb),
    cb_names
  ))) {

    stop(
      "Variance-covariance row ordering does not match crossbasis."
    )

  }

  if (any(!is.finite(beta))) {
    stop("Non-finite crossbasis coefficients detected.")
  }

  if (any(!is.finite(V_cb))) {
    stop("Non-finite crossbasis variance-covariance elements detected.")
  }

  list(
    coef = beta,
    vcov = V_cb,
    basis_names = cb_names
  )
}

```

19. Safe crosspred() function

```{r}
safe_crosspred <- function(
    cb,
    fit,
    cen,
    by = 0.1,
    cumul = TRUE
) {

  pars <- extract_crossbasis_parameters(
    cb = cb,
    fit = fit
  )

  pred <- tryCatch(

    dlnm::crosspred(
      cb,
      coef = pars$coef,
      vcov = pars$vcov,
      model.link = "log",
      cen = cen,
      by = by,
      cumul = cumul
    ),

    error = function(e) {

      stop(
        "Safe crosspred failed.\n",
        "Error: ",
        conditionMessage(e)
      )

    }
  )

  pred
}

```

20. Diagnostic function for every fitted DLNM
```{r}

diagnose_dlnm_fit <- function(
    cb,
    fit,
    label = "model"
) {

  cb_names <- colnames(cb)
  coef_names <- names(stats::coef(fit))
  V <- stats::vcov(fit)

  expected_names <- paste0(
    "cb",
    cb_names
  )

  list(
    model = label,

    crossbasis_columns =
      ncol(cb),

    model_coefficients =
      length(stats::coef(fit)),

    exact_expected_coefficients =
      all(
        expected_names %in% coef_names
      ),

    coefficient_length_match =
      length(
        stats::coef(fit)[expected_names]
      ) == ncol(cb),

    vcov_length_match =
      all(
        expected_names %in%
          rownames(V)
      ),

    finite_coefficients =
      all(
        is.finite(
          stats::coef(fit)[expected_names]
        )
      ),

    finite_vcov =
      all(
        is.finite(
          V[
            expected_names,
            expected_names,
            drop = FALSE
          ]
        )
      ),

    crossbasis_rank =
      qr(cb)$rank,

    crossbasis_full_rank =
      qr(cb)$rank == ncol(cb)
  )
}

```

21. DLNM model-fitting function

```{r}
run_dlnm_spec <- function(
    dat,
    max_lag,
    exposure_df = 3L,
    lag_df = 3L
) {

  required_lag <- paste0(
    "utci_lag",
    max_lag
  )

  if (!required_lag %in% names(dat)) {

    stop(
      "Required lag variable missing: ",
      required_lag
    )

  }

  d <- dat %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(outcome),
      !is.na(stratum_id),
      !is.na(utci_lag0),
      !is.na(.data[[required_lag]])
    ) %>%
    arrange(
      stratum_id,
      date
    )

  if (n_distinct(d$stratum_id) < 10) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  cb <- dlnm::crossbasis(

    d$utci_lag0,

    lag = max_lag,

    argvar = list(
      fun = "ns",
      df = exposure_df
    ),

    arglag = list(
      fun = "ns",
      df = lag_df
    )
  )

  fit <- tryCatch(

    gnm::gnm(

      outcome ~ cb,

      eliminate =
        factor(stratum_id),

      family =
        quasipoisson(),

      data = d,

      trace = FALSE
    ),

    error = function(e) {

      attr(
        NULL,
        "error"
      ) <- conditionMessage(e)

      NULL

    }
  )

  if (is.null(fit)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  pars <- extract_crossbasis_parameters(
    cb = cb,
    fit = fit
  )

  dispersion <- tryCatch(
    summary(fit)$dispersion,
    error = function(e)
      NA_real_
  )

  convergence <- tryCatch(
    isTRUE(fit$converged),
    error = function(e)
      TRUE
  )

  kappa_value <- tryCatch(

    kappa(
      pars$vcov
    ),

    error = function(e)
      NA_real_
  )

  list(

    fit = fit,

    cb = cb,

    data = d,

    coef_cb = pars$coef,

    vcov_cb = pars$vcov,

    max_lag = max_lag,

    exposure_df = exposure_df,

    lag_df = lag_df,

    dispersion = dispersion,

    converged = convergence,

    kappa = kappa_value

  )
}
```


22. QAIC function

Because the model is quasi-Poisson, ordinary likelihood AIC should not be reported as though the model were Poisson likelihood based.

```{r}

qaic_deviance <- function(fit) {

  dev <- tryCatch(
    deviance(fit),
    error = function(e)
      NA_real_
  )

  phi <- tryCatch(
    summary(fit)$dispersion,
    error = function(e)
      NA_real_
  )

  k <- length(
    coef(fit)
  )

  if (
    !is.finite(dev) ||
    !is.finite(phi) ||
    phi <= 0
  ) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  dev / phi + 2 * k
}

```

25. Verify safe crosspred() before proceeding

This is the critical repair for the previous error.
```{r}


prediction_test <- purrr::imap(

  fits,

  function(obj, id) {

    cen_test <- median(
      obj$data$utci_lag0,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    pred <- safe_crosspred(
      cb = obj$cb,
      fit = obj$fit,
      cen = cen_test,
      by = 0.1,
      cumul = TRUE
    )

    list(
      model_id = id,
      prediction = pred,
      cen = cen_test
    )
  }
)

prediction_validation <- tibble(

  model_id =
    names(prediction_test),

  crosspred_success =
    vapply(
      prediction_test,
      function(x)
        inherits(
          x$prediction,
          "crosspred"
        ),
      logical(1)
    )

)

flextable(prediction_validation) %>%
  autofit()

if (!all(prediction_validation$crosspred_success)) {

  stop(
    "At least one model failed the repaired crosspred compatibility test."
  )

}



```

29. Cumulative RR comparison: Lag 7 vs Lag 14 vs Lag 21

This is one of the main decision figures.

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 29. CUMULATIVE RR COMPARISON
#     LAG 7 vs LAG 14 vs LAG 21
#     ALL USING E3_L3
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Purpose
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Compare the cumulative UTCI-mortality association across
# the three prespecified lag structures:
#
#   Lag 7  : E3_L3
#   Lag 14 : E3_L3
#   Lag 21 : E3_L3
#
# IMPORTANT:
# dlnm::crosspred(..., cumul = TRUE) returns cumulative
# estimates across individual lag points.
#
# Therefore:
#
#   pred$cumRRfit
#
# is typically a matrix with:
#
#   rows    = exposure values
#   columns = cumulative lag points
#
# The final column represents the cumulative association
# through the maximum lag.
#
# This section therefore extracts ONLY the final cumulative
# RR through lag 7, lag 14, and lag 21 respectively.
# ------------------------------------------------------------


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.1 Diagnostic function for cumulative prediction objects
# ------------------------------------------------------------

diagnose_cumulative_prediction <- function(pred, label) {

  cat("\n====================================================\n")
  cat("CUMULATIVE PREDICTION CHECK:", label, "\n")
  cat("====================================================\n")

  cat("Length predvar:",
      length(pred$predvar), "\n")

  cat("Dimensions cumRRfit:")

  print(dim(pred$cumRRfit))

  cat("Dimensions cumRRlow:")

  print(dim(pred$cumRRlow))

  cat("Dimensions cumRRhigh:")

  print(dim(pred$cumRRhigh))

  if (is.matrix(pred$cumRRfit)) {

    cat(
      "Number of exposure values:",
      nrow(pred$cumRRfit),
      "\n"
    )

    cat(
      "Number of cumulative lag points:",
      ncol(pred$cumRRfit),
      "\n"
    )

  } else {

    cat(
      "cumRRfit is not a matrix.\n"
    )

  }

  cat("====================================================\n")
}


# Run diagnostics before extraction

diagnose_cumulative_prediction(
  pred_lag7,
  "Lag 7 E3_L3"
)

diagnose_cumulative_prediction(
  pred_lag14,
  "Lag 14 E3_L3"
)

diagnose_cumulative_prediction(
  pred_lag21,
  "Lag 21 E3_L3"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.2 Robust extraction function
# ------------------------------------------------------------

extract_final_cumulative_rr <- function(
    pred,
    label,
    max_lag
) {

  exposure <- as.numeric(pred$predvar)

  rr <- pred$cumRRfit
  low <- pred$cumRRlow
  high <- pred$cumRRhigh


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Handle matrix output from crosspred()
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (is.matrix(rr)) {

    # Final column = cumulative association through
    # the maximum lag represented in the prediction object.

    rr_final <- rr[, ncol(rr)]

    low_final <- low[, ncol(low)]

    high_final <- high[, ncol(high)]

  } else {

    # Fallback in case crosspred returns vectors

    rr_final <- as.numeric(rr)

    low_final <- as.numeric(low)

    high_final <- as.numeric(high)

  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Strict dimensional validation
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (
    length(exposure) != length(rr_final) ||
    length(exposure) != length(low_final) ||
    length(exposure) != length(high_final)
  ) {

    stop(
      "\nCumulative RR extraction failed for ",
      label,
      ".\n",
      "Exposure length = ", length(exposure), "\n",
      "RR length = ", length(rr_final), "\n",
      "Lower CI length = ", length(low_final), "\n",
      "Upper CI length = ", length(high_final), "\n",
      "Check the crosspred object before proceeding."
    )

  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Return clean long-format data
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  tibble(
    exposure = exposure,
    RR = as.numeric(rr_final),
    low = as.numeric(low_final),
    high = as.numeric(high_final),
    max_lag = max_lag,
    model = label
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.3 Extract the three cumulative curves
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cum_rr_lag7 <- extract_final_cumulative_rr(
  pred = pred_lag7,
  label = "Lag 7 E3_L3",
  max_lag = 7
)


cum_rr_lag14 <- extract_final_cumulative_rr(
  pred = pred_lag14,
  label = "Lag 14 E3_L3",
  max_lag = 14
)


cum_rr_lag21 <- extract_final_cumulative_rr(
  pred = pred_lag21,
  label = "Lag 21 E3_L3",
  max_lag = 21
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.4 Combine
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cum_rr <- bind_rows(
  cum_rr_lag7,
  cum_rr_lag14,
  cum_rr_lag21
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.5 Final validation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(
  nrow(cum_rr_lag7) > 0,
  nrow(cum_rr_lag14) > 0,
  nrow(cum_rr_lag21) > 0
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    is.finite(cum_rr$exposure) |
      is.na(cum_rr$exposure)
  )
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    is.finite(cum_rr$RR) |
      is.na(cum_rr$RR)
  )
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    is.finite(cum_rr$low) |
      is.na(cum_rr$low)
  )
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    is.finite(cum_rr$high) |
      is.na(cum_rr$high)
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.6 Check number of observations per curve
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cum_rr %>%
  group_by(model, max_lag) %>%
  summarise(
    n_exposure = n(),
    exposure_min = min(exposure, na.rm = TRUE),
    exposure_max = max(exposure, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.7 Plot cumulative RR curves
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_cumulative_rr <- ggplot(
  cum_rr,
  aes(
    x = exposure,
    y = RR,
    linetype = model
  )
) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = low,
      ymax = high,
      group = model
    ),
    alpha = 0.10,
    colour = NA
  ) +

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +

  labs(
    title =
      "Cumulative UTCI–mortality relative risk",

    subtitle =
      "Comparison of prespecified E3_L3 lag structures",

    x =
      "Mean UTCI (°C)",

    y =
      "Cumulative relative risk",

    linetype =
      "Maximum lag"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 12
  )


p_cumulative_rr


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.8 Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

dir.create(
  "Results/LagComparison",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


ggsave(
  filename =
    "Results/LagComparison/Figure_Cumulative_RR_Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3.png",

  plot =
    p_cumulative_rr,

  width = 11,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.9 Save analytical dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

write_csv(
  cum_rr,
  "Results/LagComparison/Cumulative_RR_Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3.csv"
)


saveRDS(
  cum_rr,
  "Results/LagComparison/Cumulative_RR_Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3.rds"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 29.10 Display the final cumulative RR values at selected
#       exposure percentiles
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cum_rr_summary <- cum_rr %>%

  group_by(model, max_lag) %>%

  summarise(

    minimum_exposure =
      min(exposure, na.rm = TRUE),

    median_exposure =
      median(exposure, na.rm = TRUE),

    maximum_exposure =
      max(exposure, na.rm = TRUE),

    minimum_RR =
      min(RR, na.rm = TRUE),

    maximum_RR =
      max(RR, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"

  )


cum_rr_summary


write_csv(
  cum_rr_summary,
  "Results/LagComparison/Cumulative_RR_Summary_Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3.csv"
)
```

30. Lag-response curves

The values are snapped to the actual prediction grid to avoid the floating-point issue encountered previously.

```{r}

nearest_prediction_value <- function(
    pred,
    value
) {

  pred$predvar[
    which.min(
      abs(
        pred$predvar -
          value
      )
    )
  ]
}

plot_lag_response_safe <- function(
    pred,
    at,
    title
) {

  at_use <-
    nearest_prediction_value(
      pred,
      at
    )

  dlnm::plot.crosspred(
    pred,
    "slices",
    var = at_use,
    ci = "lines",
    xlab = "Lag (days)",
    ylab = "Relative risk",
    main =
      paste0(
        title,
        "\nUTCI = ",
        round(at_use, 1),
        " °C"
      )
  )
}

```

35. Lag-specific effects and harvesting assessment

The cumulative effect over a lag window is calculated as the exponential of the sum of the lag-specific log-relative-risks.
```{r}


summarise_lag_windows <- function(
    pred,
    at,
    max_lag,
    label
) {

  at_use <-
    nearest_prediction_value(
      pred,
      at
    )

  exposure_index <-
    which(
      pred$predvar ==
        at_use
    )

  log_rr <-
    log(
      pred$matRRfit[
        exposure_index,
        1:(max_lag + 1)
      ]
    )

  lag_days <-
    0:max_lag

  windows <- list(

    Immediate =
      c(0, 0),

    Short =
      c(1, min(3, max_lag)),

    Medium =
      c(4, min(7, max_lag)),

    Delayed =
      c(8, min(14, max_lag)),

    Harvesting =
      c(min(15, max_lag), max_lag)

  )

  purrr::imap_dfr(

    windows,

    function(rng, window_name) {

      if (rng[1] > rng[2]) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      selected <-
        lag_days >= rng[1] &
        lag_days <= rng[2]

      tibble(

        exposure_condition = label,

        window = window_name,

        lag_range =
          paste0(
            rng[1],
            "–",
            rng[2]
          ),

        cumulative_RR =
          exp(
            sum(
              log_rr[selected],
              na.rm = TRUE
            )
          )

      )
    }
  )
}

```

37. Specifically evaluate the additional Lag 15–21 contribution

This is important for deciding whether Lag 21 is adding meaningful delayed information or mainly extending the model into a harvesting period.


```{r}
lag15_21_summary <- function(pred) {

  if (max(pred$lag) < 21) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  idx_15_21 <-
    16:22

  tibble(

    exposure =
      pred$predvar,

    incremental_RR_15_21 =
      exp(
        rowSums(
          log(
            pred$matRRfit[
              ,
              idx_15_21
            ]
          ),
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      )

  )
}
```

```{r}
      ),

      qaic_deviance(
        fit_lag21_e3_l3$fit
      )
    ),

  Dispersion =
    c(
      fit_lag7_e3_l3$dispersion,
      fit_lag14_e3_l3$dispersion,
      fit_lag21_e3_l3$dispersion
    ),

  Kappa =
    c(
      fit_lag7_e3_l3$kappa,
      fit_lag14_e3_l3$kappa,
      fit_lag21_e3_l3$kappa
    )

)

flextable(lag_decision_table) %>%
  colformat_num(
    digits = 3
  ) %>%
  autofit()

write_csv(
  lag_decision_table,
  "Results/LagComparison/Table_Lag_Decision_Pre_Lock.csv"
)

```

39. Manual primary-lag decision gate

Do not automatically choose the lag.

This is deliberately left to the investigator after inspecting the empirical outputs.


```{r}

if (!is.null(PRIMARY_LAG)) {

  if (!PRIMARY_LAG %in% c(7, 14, 21)) {

    stop(
      "PRIMARY_LAG must be 7, 14 or 21."
    )

  }

  message(

} else {

    "5. Lag 21 3D surface\n",

}
```

40. Manual primary-lag selection block

When you are ready, change only this section:

```{r}

# ============================================================
# MANUAL PRIMARY LAG SELECTION
# ============================================================

# PRIMARY_LAG <- 7

# PRIMARY_LAG <- 14

# PRIMARY_LAG <- 21
```



The recommendation is not to choose based on the smallest QAIC alone.

The decision should consider:

biological plausibility;
stability of the exposure-response curve;
stability of the lag-response structure;
cumulative RR;
whether additional lags contribute meaningfully;
whether Lag 15–21 appears to represent delayed effect or harvesting;
model diagnostics;
interpretability;
consistency with the prespecified epidemiological objective.

```{r}

  mmt_index <-
    which.min(
      primary_pred$allRRfit

  PRIMARY_MMT <-
```

45. Memory-safe uncertainty for MMT and nonlinear derived quantities
Important methodological update

Do not run:

for (b in 1:1000) {
    resample_data()
    refit_gnm()
}

on this 186,628-row case-crossover dataset.

That approach repeatedly constructs large model matrices and repeatedly fits conditional quasi-Poisson models. It is unnecessarily expensive and can cause memory exhaustion.

Instead, the preferred calculation here is parametric Monte Carlo simulation from the fitted coefficient vector and its variance-covariance matrix.

The original analysis framework already adopted this approach specifically to avoid repeated model refitting.

The implementation below is additionally memory-conscious:

simulations are processed in chunks;
the complete nsim × prediction-grid matrix is never required;
only the quantities needed for the MMT distribution are retained;
Cholesky decomposition is calculated once;
the random coefficient draws are generated in manageable batches.

```{r}
mmt_mc_uncertainty <- function(

    cb,

    fit,

    exposure_data,

    lower_quantile = 0.05,

    upper_quantile = 0.95,

    by = 0.1,

    nsim = 10000,

    chunk_size = 250,

    seed = 1

) {

  set.seed(seed)

  pars <-
    extract_crossbasis_parameters(
      cb,
      fit
    )

  beta <-
    as.numeric(
      pars$coef
    )

  V <-
    as.matrix(
      pars$vcov
    )

  p <-
    length(beta)

  exposure_limits <-
    quantile(
      exposure_data,
      c(
        lower_quantile,
        upper_quantile
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

  base_pred <-
    dlnm::crosspred(
      cb,
      coef = pars$coef,
      vcov = pars$vcov,
      model.link = "log",
      by = by,
      cumul = TRUE
    )

  grid <-
    as.numeric(
      base_pred$predvar
    )

  keep <-
    grid >= exposure_limits[1] &
    grid <= exposure_limits[2]

  grid_use <-
    grid[keep]

  # ------------------------------------------
  # Stable Cholesky decomposition
  # ------------------------------------------

  eig <-
    eigen(
      V,
      symmetric = TRUE
    )

  eig$values[
    eig$values < 0
  ] <- 0

  root_V <-
    eig$vectors %*%
    diag(
      sqrt(
        eig$values
      ),
      nrow = p
    )

  # ------------------------------------------
  # Storage only for MMT
  # ------------------------------------------

  mmt_values <-
    rep(
      NA_real_,
      nsim
    )

  # Optional storage of selected tail predictions
  # only, rather than the complete prediction matrix.

  target_exposures <-
    c(
      quantile(
        exposure_data,
        c(
          .01,
          .05,
          .95,
          .99
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    )

  target_indices <-
    vapply(

      target_exposures,

      function(x)
        which.min(
          abs(
            grid -
              x
          )
        ),

      integer(1)

    )

  target_draws <-
    matrix(
      NA_real_,
      nrow = nsim,
      ncol = length(
        target_indices
      )
    )

  # ------------------------------------------
  # Prediction matrix for exposure-response
  # ------------------------------------------

  full_base <-
    dlnm::crosspred(
      cb,
      coef = pars$coef,
      vcov = pars$vcov,
      model.link = "log",
      by = by,
      cumul = TRUE
    )

  # matfit is the linear predictor contribution
  # for each exposure and lag combination.
  #
  # For MMT we require the overall cumulative
  # exposure-response coefficient vector.

  overall_basis <-
    full_base$matfit

  # ------------------------------------------
  # Simulation in chunks
  # ------------------------------------------

  starts <-
    seq(
      1,
      nsim,
      by = chunk_size
    )

  for (start_i in starts) {

    end_i <-
      min(
        start_i +
          chunk_size -
          1,
        nsim
      )

    n_chunk <-
      end_i -
      start_i +
      1

    Z <-
      matrix(
        rnorm(
          n_chunk *
            p
        ),
        nrow = n_chunk,
        ncol = p
      )

    beta_sim <-
      sweep(
        Z %*% t(root_V),
        2,
        beta,
        "+"
      )

    # ----------------------------------------
    # Reconstruct cumulative exposure-response
    # ----------------------------------------

    # The crosspred object stores the prediction
    # basis through its coefficient-space representation.
    #
    # Reconstruct using the crossbasis prediction
    # matrices generated by crosspred.

    chunk_rr <-
      matrix(
        NA_real_,
        nrow = n_chunk,
        ncol = length(
          grid
        )
      )

    for (j in seq_along(grid)) {

      # Overall cumulative coefficient vector
      # represented by the corresponding row
      # of the prediction matrix.

      basis_row <-
        full_base$matfit[j, ]

      chunk_rr[, j] <-
        exp(
          beta_sim %*%
            basis_row
        )

    }

    # ----------------------------------------
    # MMT from grid
    # ----------------------------------------

    selected_rr <-
      chunk_rr[, keep, drop = FALSE]

    local_mmt <-
      apply(
        selected_rr,
        1,
        function(x)
          grid_use[
            which.min(x)
          ]
      )

    mmt_values[
      start_i:end_i
    ] <-
      local_mmt

    target_draws[
      start_i:end_i,
      ] <-
      chunk_rr[
        ,
        target_indices,
        drop = FALSE
      ]

    rm(
      Z,
      beta_sim,
      chunk_rr,
      selected_rr,
      local_mmt
    )

    gc(
      verbose = FALSE
    )
  }

  list(

    mmt =
      mmt_values,

    mmt_ci =
      quantile(
        mmt_values,
        c(
          0.025,
          0.975
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    target_exposures =
      target_exposures,

    target_rr =
      target_draws,

    grid =
      grid,

    seed =
      seed,

    nsim =
      nsim

  )
}

```

```{r}
      ),

    MMT_lower_95 =
```

49. Primary model cumulative RR at clinically meaningful contrasts

Do not assume arbitrary clinical cut-offs. Use empirical percentile contrasts around the MMT unless the protocol separately specifies clinically meaningful thresholds.


```{r}
if (!is.null(primary_pred)) {

  exposure_quantiles <-
    quantile(
      primary_fit$data$utci_lag0,
      c(
        .01,
        .05,
        .50,
        .95,
        .99
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

  primary_contrast_table <-
    tibble(

      Exposure_label =
        c(
          "P01",
          "P05",
          "Median",
          "P95",
          "P99"
        ),

      UTCI =
        as.numeric(
          exposure_quantiles
        )

    ) %>%

    mutate(

      grid_value =
        map_dbl(
          UTCI,
          ~ nearest_prediction_value(
            primary_pred,
            .x
          )
        )

    ) %>%

    mutate(

      Cumulative_RR =
        map_dbl(
          grid_value,
          ~ primary_pred$cumRRfit[
            which(
              primary_pred$predvar ==
                .x
            )
          ]
        ),

      Lower_95 =
        map_dbl(
          grid_value,
          ~ primary_pred$cumRRlow[
            which(
              primary_pred$predvar ==
                .x
            )
          ]
        ),

      Upper_95 =
        map_dbl(
          grid_value,
          ~ primary_pred$cumRRhigh[
            which(
              primary_pred$predvar ==
                .x
            )
          ]
        )

    )

  flextable(
    primary_contrast_table
  ) %>%
    colformat_num(
      digits = 3
    ) %>%
    autofit()

  write_csv(
    primary_contrast_table,
    paste0(
      "Results/PrimaryModel/Table_Primary_Cumulative_RR_Lag",
      PRIMARY_LAG,
      ".csv"
    )
  )

}

```

51. Objective 3: temporal-period analysis

The actual observed years in the processed data must be used. Do not silently impose a period that is absent from the dataset.
```{r}


observed_years <- sort(
  unique(
    model_data$year
  )
)

observed_year_range <- range(
  observed_years,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

tibble(
  First_year = observed_year_range[1],
  Last_year = observed_year_range[2],
  Number_of_years = length(observed_years)
) %>%
  flextable() %>%
  autofit()


The following creates data-driven early/late periods only if there are sufficient years to support them.


if (
  length(observed_years) >= 4
) {

  midpoint_year <-
    floor(
      mean(
        observed_year_range
      )
    )

  periods <- list(

    Early =
      c(
        observed_year_range[1],
        midpoint_year
      ),

    Late =
      c(
        midpoint_year + 1,
        observed_year_range[2]
      )

  )

} else {

  periods <- NULL

}
```


52. Temporal model fitting
```{r}

temporal_results <- NULL

if (!is.null(periods) &&
    !is.null(primary_fit)) {

  temporal_results <-
    purrr::imap(

      periods,

      function(period_range, period_name) {

        period_data <-
          model_data %>%
          filter(
            year >= period_range[1],
            year <= period_range[2]
          )

        if (
          n_distinct(
            period_data$stratum_id
          ) < 20
        ) {
          return(NULL)
        }

        run_dlnm_spec(
          period_data,
          max_lag =
            PRIMARY_LAG,
          exposure_df = 3,
          lag_df = 3
        )

      }

    )

  names(
    temporal_results
  ) <-
    names(periods)

}

```

56. Subgroup prediction curves

```{r}
plot_subgroup_predictions <- function(
    results_list,
    filename,
    title
) {

  valid_results <-
    results_list[
      !vapply(
        results_list,
        is.null,
        logical(1)
      )
    ]

  if (
    length(valid_results) == 0
  ) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  curves <-
    purrr::imap_dfr(

      valid_results,

      function(obj, label) {

        pred <-
          safe_crosspred(
            obj$cb,
            obj$fit,
            cen = COMMON_CEN,
            by = .1,
            cumul = TRUE
          )

        tibble(

          exposure =
            pred$predvar,

          RR =
            pred$allRRfit,

          low =
            pred$allRRlow,

          high =
            pred$allRRhigh,

          subgroup =
            label

        )

      }

    )

  p <-
    ggplot(
      curves,
      aes(
        exposure,
        RR,
        linetype = subgroup
      )
    ) +

    geom_hline(
      yintercept = 1,
      linewidth = .4
    ) +

    geom_line(
      linewidth = .8
    ) +

    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Mean UTCI (°C)",
      y = "Cumulative relative risk",
      linetype = "Subgroup"
    ) +

    theme_minimal(
      base_size = 12
    )

  p

  ggsave(
    filename,
    p,
    width = 10,
    height = 7,
    dpi = 300
  )

  invisible(
    p
  )
}

```

65. Final validation checklist

```{r}
validation <- tibble(

  Check =
    c(

      "Analytical dataset imported",

      "Required variables present",

      "Outcome is binary",

      "One case per stratum",

      "At least one referent per stratum",

      "UTCI lag 0 available",

      "UTCI lag 7 available",

      "UTCI lag 14 available",

      "UTCI lag 21 available",

      "Lag 7 model fitted",

      "Lag 14 model fitted",

      "Lag 21 model fitted",

      "Crossbasis coefficient compatibility verified",

      "Crossbasis vcov compatibility verified",

      "Safe crosspred successful",

      "Cumulative RR comparison generated",

      "3D Lag 7 surface generated",

      "3D Lag 14 surface generated",

      "3D Lag 21 surface generated",

      "Primary lag manually locked"

    ),

  Status =
    c(

      TRUE,

      length(missing_variables) == 0,

      all(
        model_data$outcome %in%
          c(0, 1)
      ),

      all(
        stratum_qc$n_cases == 1
      ),

      all(
        stratum_qc$n_referents >= 1
      ),

      all(
        !is.na(
          model_data$utci_lag0
        )
      ),

      all(
        !is.na(
          model_data$utci_lag7
        )
      ),

      all(
        !is.na(
          model_data$utci_lag14
        )
      ),

      all(
        !is.na(
          model_data$utci_lag21
        )
      ),

      !is.null(
        fit_lag7_e3_l3
      ),

      !is.null(
        fit_lag14_e3_l3
      ),

      !is.null(
        fit_lag21_e3_l3
      ),

      all(
        candidate_diagnostics$coefficients_match
      ),

      all(
        candidate_diagnostics$vcov_match
      ),

      all(
        prediction_validation$crosspred_success
      ),

      file.exists(
        "Results/LagComparison/Figure_Cumulative_RR_Lag7_Lag14_Lag21_E3_L3.png"
      ),

      file.exists(
        "Results/LagComparison/Figure_3D_Lag7_E3_L3.png"
      ),

      file.exists(
        "Results/LagComparison/Figure_3D_Lag14_E3_L3.png"
      ),

      file.exists(
        "Results/LagComparison/Figure_3D_Lag21_E3_L3.png"
      ),

      !is.null(
        PRIMARY_LAG
      )

    )

)

flextable(
  validation
) %>%
  autofit()

write_csv(
  validation,
  "Results/Diagnostics/Final_Validation_Checklist.csv"
)

if (
  !all(
    validation$Status[
      -nrow(validation)
    ]
  )
) {

  warning(
    "One or more non-primary validation checks failed. ",
    "Inspect Final_Validation_Checklist.csv."
  )

}
```
